definitions.explanation: The large innermost toe on the foot. In Japanese, toes are usually referred to using the names of the fingers of the hand prefixed with {足|あし}の ('of the foot'), so the big toe is literally 'the thumb of the foot.' Frequently mentioned in medical, sports, and footwear contexts.

examples.japanese: {足|あし}の{親指|おやゆび}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{痛|いた}い→痛い：01108_itai⟧。
⟦{靴|くつ}→靴：00725_kutsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{小|ちい}さくて→小さい：00025_chiisai⟧、{足|あし}の{親指|おやゆび}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{当|あ}たる→当たる：01860_ataru⟧。
examples.english: The shoes are small, and they're pressing against my big toe.

examples.japanese: ⟦{階段|かいだん}→階段：00782_kaidan⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{足|あし}の{親指|おやゆび}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{爪|つめ}→爪：02159_tsume⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦ぶつけて→ぶつける：02413_butsukeru⟧しまった。
examples.english: I bumped the toenail of my big toe on the stairs.

examples.japanese: {足|あし}の{親指|おやゆび}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{付|つ}け{根|ね}→付け根：11681_tsukene⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{腫|は}れて→腫れる：12325_hareru⟧、⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧つらい。
examples.english: The base of my big toe is swollen, and even walking is painful.

notes:
Literally 'the thumb of the foot.' Japanese does not have distinct one-word names for each toe; instead, toes are described by taking the corresponding finger name and prefixing it with ⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧.

TOE NAMES:
- {足|あし}の{親指|おやゆび}: big toe (= thumb of foot)
- ⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人差|ひとさ}し{指|ゆび}→人差し指：11471_hitosashiyubi⟧: second toe (= index finger of foot)
- ⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中指|なかゆび}→中指：04281_nakayubi⟧: middle toe
- ⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{薬指|くすりゆび}→薬指：16373_kusuriyubi⟧: fourth toe (= ring finger of foot)
- ⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{小指|こゆび}→小指：04029_koyubi⟧: little toe

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {足|あし}の{親指|おやゆび}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦ぶつける→ぶつける：02413_butsukeru⟧: to stub one's big toe
- {足|あし}の{親指|おやゆび}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{爪|つめ}→爪：02159_tsume⟧: the nail of the big toe
- {足|あし}の{親指|おやゆび}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{付|つ}け{根|ね}→付け根：11681_tsukene⟧: the base of the big toe
- {足|あし}の{親指|おやゆび}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{痛|いた}い→痛い：01108_itai⟧: one's big toe hurts
- {足|あし}の{親指|おやゆび}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{骨折|こっせつ}→骨折：02763_kossetsu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to break one's big toe

USAGE:
- In everyday speech, people often just say ⟦{親指|おやゆび}→親指：04114_oyayubi⟧ when context makes it clear whether the hand or foot is meant — e.g., when pointing to one's foot or discussing shoes.
- The technical medical term is {母趾|ぼし} or {第一趾|だいいっし}, but these are rarely used outside hospitals.
- Common medical conditions named with this word include {巻|ま}き{爪|づめ} ('ingrown toenail') and {外反母趾|がいはんぼし} ('bunion; hallux valgus').
